growth_problem: Webinars produce the most leads and the strongest lead-to-MQL conversion, but most webinar MQLs never become sales-qualified, so webinar volume is not turning into pipeline.

hypotheses.title: Webinar leads are learners, not buyers
hypotheses.observed_problem: Webinar leads become MQLs readily but sales rejects most of them.
hypotheses.causal_explanation: The MQL rules reward webinar attendance, so contacts without budget, authority, or an active project reach sales.
hypotheses.intervention: Add buying-intent questions to registration and require an intent signal before MQL.
hypotheses.expected_behavior_change: Fewer but better webinar MQLs; sales accepts a much larger share.
hypotheses.expected_business_outcome: More SQLs per sales hour and steady webinar-sourced pipeline.

supporting.claim: Webinar MQL to SQL conversion is far below other sources on large volume.
Most webinar rejections cite budget, authority, or student status.
Webinars convert leads to MQL better than any source but fail downstream.
Webinars are the largest lead source with the lowest lead-to-win rate.
Webinar attendees describe learning or research with no project or budget.

missing: How the MQL score weights webinar attendance.
Whether rejected webinar contacts convert later through nurture.

hypotheses.title: Accepted webinar SQLs stall at the sales handoff
hypotheses.observed_problem: Even the webinar leads that sales accepts convert to opportunities less often than others.
hypotheses.causal_explanation: Sales treats webinar SQLs as lower priority and follows up with generic outreach.
hypotheses.intervention: Give accepted webinar SQLs the same discovery-call playbook as demo requests.
hypotheses.expected_behavior_change: More accepted webinar SQLs reach a scheduled discovery call.
hypotheses.expected_business_outcome: Higher webinar SQL to opportunity conversion.

supporting.claim: Webinar SQL to opportunity conversion is below other sources.

contradicting.claim: Most of the webinar loss happens before the handoff, at qualification, so the handoff is a secondary leak at most.

missing: Sales activity data for accepted webinar SQLs.
Opportunity notes on why webinar SQLs stall.

action_detail: Add intent questions to webinar registration and require an intent signal before MQL; route the rest to nurture.
guardrail_metric: Webinar-sourced qualified pipeline must not fall.
downstream_metric: Webinar SQL to opportunity and win rate.
learning_objective: Learn whether intent screening fixes webinar lead quality without shrinking real demand.
missing_evidence: MQL scoring rules and their weights.
